facts.fact_text: The opposition planned to hold a demonstration on 17 November 2012 in Baku.
The opposition planned to hold a demonstration on 26 January 2013 in Baku.
The applicant attended the demonstration of 17 November 2012.
The applicant attended the demonstration of 26 January 2013.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations were conducted in a peaceful manner.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation of the demonstration of 17 November 2012.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation of the demonstration of 26 January 2013.
Shortly after the demonstration of 17 November 2012 had begun, the police started to disperse it.
Shortly after the demonstration of 26 January 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse it.
The Baku City Executive Authority refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration of 17 November 2012.
The Baku City Executive Authority stated in general terms that the demonstration of 17 November 2012 was not in accordance with the Law on Freedom of Assembly.
The Baku City Executive Authority stated that the square where the organisers proposed to hold the assembly of 17 November 2012 was a designated public leisure area.
The Baku City Executive Authority stated that the assembly of 17 November 2012 was impractical.
At the time of both of the applicant's arrests, under Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 17 November 2012, Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 provided that any breach of the rules, set forth under the legislation, on the organisation and holding of assemblies, demonstrations, protests, marches and pickets shall be punishable by a reprimand or a fine of seven to thirteen Azerbaijani manats.

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 17 November 2012, Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 provided that deliberate failure by an individual to comply with a lawful order of a police officer or military serviceman carrying out their duties to protect public order shall be punishable by a fine of twenty to twenty-five Azerbaijani manats or, if that sanction is inadequate in the circumstances of the case and taking into account the character of the offender, by administrative detention for a term of up to fifteen days.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 entered into force on 1 January 2013.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced new wording to Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences concerning breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies.

Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies became explicitly punishable under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced for the first time a punishment in the form of administrative detention of up to fifteen days for breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
Shortly after the demonstration of 17 November 2012 had begun, the police started to disperse it.
Shortly after the demonstration of 26 January 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse it.
The Baku City Executive Authority refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration of 17 November 2012.
The Baku City Executive Authority stated in general terms that the demonstration of 17 November 2012 was not in accordance with the Law on Freedom of Assembly.
The Baku City Executive Authority stated that the square where the organisers proposed to hold the assembly of 17 November 2012 was a designated public leisure area.
The Baku City Executive Authority stated that the assembly of 17 November 2012 was impractical.
By a decision of 17 November 2012, the Sabail District Court convicted the applicant under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
By a decision of 17 November 2012, the Sabail District Court sentenced the applicant to five days' administrative detention.
By a decision of 26 January 2013, the Sabail District Court convicted the applicant under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
By a decision of 26 January 2013, the Sabail District Court sentenced the applicant to a fine of 500 Azerbaijani manats (AZN).

According to the applicant, members of the public were not allowed to attend the court hearings in either case, even though the court had not taken a formal decision to close the hearings to the public.

The record of the court hearing in the first case (17 November 2012) before the Sabail District Court shows that the applicant declared that he did not need legal assistance and would defend himself in person.
At the hearing in the first case (17 November 2012) before the Sabail District Court, the court did not question any witnesses.
In the second case (26 January 2013) before the Sabail District Court, the court questioned two police officers.
According to the applicant, in neither the first case (17 November 2012) nor the second case (26 January 2013) was he given access to a lawyer after his arrest or while in police custody.
According to the applicant, in neither the first case (17 November 2012) nor the second case (26 January 2013) was he given an opportunity to hire a lawyer of his own choice.
